name: Lume whole body deodorant

lead: Lume is a deodorant brand marketing a mandelic acid formula for the whole body rather than just the underarms. It gained attention on short-video platforms.
No published study has tested it, so claims rest on the manufacturer and user reports.

paras: It is a deodorant, so it targets odour-causing bacteria rather than sweat. Acid-based products are described as keeping skin mildly acidic.
Possible skin irritation, particularly on sensitive or freshly shaved skin. Regulated as a cosmetic in the US; no product-specific safety trials were found.

lead: Lume is a deodorant brand that markets a "whole body" deodorant, intended for use beyond the underarms, built on an acid-based formula using mandelic acid.[1][2] The product became widely discussed on short-video platforms, and is the best-known example of a wider trend toward non-aluminium, acid-based deodorants.

As a deodorant, it is aimed at odour rather than sweat. Body odour arises mainly from bacteria breaking down secretions of the apocrine sweat glands, concentrated in the armpits.[3] In the US, deodorants are regulated as cosmetics, while antiperspirants are regulated as drugs.[4]
Source material for this entry is limited to the manufacturer's site and general reference works. No published clinical trials of Lume were found.

paras: Lume presents its product as a deodorant for the whole body, a positioning that distinguishes it from underarm-only products.[1] The central ingredient, mandelic acid, is an alpha hydroxy acid first isolated in 1831 and also used in superficial chemical peels.[2]

sections.h: How it is described to work
paras: Acid-based deodorants are intended to keep the skin surface mildly acidic, which is said to limit bacterial growth, in contrast to alkaline products.[4] They do not stop sweating, unlike aluminium antiperspirants, which form plugs in sweat ducts.[4]

No Lume-specific safety studies were located. Reference sources note that deodorant ingredients can irritate skin in some users, for example propylene glycol or zirconium-containing antiperspirants.[4] Acids may also irritate sensitive or freshly shaved skin.

lore.intro: Lume spread largely through short-video platforms and social media, where it is described as a whole-body odour product. No forum material was available for this entry.

claims.claim: A deodorant can be used on the whole body, not just the underarms
